top_choice_rationale: P001 awards one bounded invention, magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms in an optical lattice, to Katori (concept and first realisation) and Ye (record accuracy and stability). It has a measured outcome near 1e-18, independently reproduced in several national laboratories, and realised consequences in tests of constants and relativity and in relativistic geodesy. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation can name the lattice mechanism to separate it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes. The novelty-versus-refinement reservation is real but answerable, so a prize is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: No documented connection to Katori or Ye in the profile; as a theoretical atomic physicist with collaborations in attosecond and precision atomic physics (Lund, ETH Zurich groups), a field-proximity disclosure may be warranted, but no recusal-triggering relationship is apparent from the profile.
